scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #7115: Hi, weird one: my computer, PC15 in Location B, refuses
to talk to my desk-mate's computer, PC16, even though we sit RIGHT NEXT to
each other. Nothing goes through AT ALL, in either direction. Something around
PC16's port on the office switch must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could
someone look at whatever connects our two computers and make them friends
again? We need to share files for Friday!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. PC15 and PC16 are both on the Location B
  172.18.51.0/24 subnet, in the same broadcast domain -- a pure intra-subnet,
  Layer-2 path that does not involve router6 routing. PC15 reaches PC16 with 0%
  loss; the Location B switch forwards frames normally and PC16's port is up. The
  correct answer is is_anomaly=false. (Note: this is intra-Location-B traffic,
  which is NOT subject to the router6 ACL 110 -- that policy only restricts
  Location A -> Location B, not B-internal traffic.) This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an L2/switch fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC15 cannot reach its
same-subnet Location B neighbor PC16 -- is NOT reproducible: both hosts sit on
172.18.51.0/24 in the same broadcast domain, and PC15 reaches PC16 directly (same
subnet, no routing) with 0% loss. The Location B switch forwards frames normally
and PC16's port is up. The router6 ACL 110 is irrelevant here -- it only limits
Location A -> Location B, not traffic internal to Location B.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the intra-subnet L2 path is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC15->PC16
path, finds it working, confirms both interfaces are up on the same subnet, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a switch drop, a downed port, or
(mistakenly) invokes the router6 ACL for B-internal traffic is over-diagnosing.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC15 and PC16 are same-subnet (172.18.51.0/24) within Location B and reach each other with 0% loss at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The iptables FORWARD chain on router6, specifically applied to its `eth2` interface — the WAN link (`r6_r3`) that connects router6 to router3.

**Mechanism:** Three injected DROP rules in the FORWARD chain (`-A FORWARD -i eth2 -p tcp -j DROP`, `-A FORWARD -i eth2 -p udp -j DROP`, `-A FORWARD -i eth2 -j DROP`) silently discard every TCP, UDP, and all-protocol packet that enters router6 from the router3 side. The all-protocol rule has an active hit counter of 26 packets/2184 bytes, confirming live traffic is being dropped. Because the rules match on `in-interface eth2`, they block the **return path** for traffic originating from router6's mswitch2 domain (PC15–PC18, 172.18.51.x) trying to reach router3's domain (PC11–PC14, 192.168.200.x via router4), as well as **any forward traffic** from router3's domain toward the mswitch2 domain.

**Localization:** router6, interface eth2 (`r6_r3` link), iptables FORWARD chain.

**Note on the user complaint:** PC15 and PC16 sit on the same L2 segment (switch10 → mswitch2) and communicate directly without traversing router6's eth2 — their pings succeed with 0% loss in both directions. The ticket mislocalised the fault; the real breakage is inter-area routing across the router6↔router3 WAN link.

**Root cause:** Injected iptables DROP rules on router6's eth2 block all forwarded transit traffic, severing bidirectional routing between the router3/router4 (PC11–PC14) domain and the router6/mswitch2 (PC15–PC18) domain.

**Fix:** Remove the three DROP rules from router6's FORWARD chain: `iptables -D FORWARD -i eth2 -p tcp -j DROP`, `iptables -D FORWARD -i eth2 -p udp -j DROP`, and `iptables -D FORWARD -i eth2 -j DROP`.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC15 and PC16 are same-subnet (172.18.51.0/24) within Location B and reach each other with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly notes PC15 and PC16 are on the same L2/subnet (172.18.51.x) and that pings between them succeed with 0% loss, matching the baseline healthy note.

The agent's investigation log contains direct, relevant observations (successful intra-subnet pings, cross-subnet timeouts, infra_sweep flag, and iptables FORWARD rules with hit counts) that support the conclusion that router6's FORWARD chain on eth2 is dropping forwarded traffic. The inference chain is logical and the essential checks to distinguish intra-subnet vs inter-subnet problems were performed.

The inference chain is logical and the essential checks to distinguish intra-subnet vs inter-subnet problems were performed.
